strings.name: Robert Shiller
strings.summary: Shiller studies asset prices, bubbles and behavioural finance, challenging simple rational-expectations explanations of market prices. He helped build house-price indices and developed narrative economics to examine how stories shape collective decisions. A 2013 economics Nobel co-laureate, he is now a Yale emeritus professor and contributes to debate on confidence and policy.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Prices and psychology
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses volatility evidence to challenge simplified efficient-market accounts, emphasizing beliefs and social transmission.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Indices and institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Builds housing data with collaborators and studies tools for sharing economic risk.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Tariff-interview report published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Warned that policy reversals could weaken confidence and raise economic risk; these were his contemporary judgments.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Narrative Economics published
strings.timeline.t2.text: Examined how circulating stories affect behaviour and major economic events.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won with Eugene Fama and Lars Peter Hansen for empirical asset-price analysis.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Irrational Exuberance published
strings.timeline.t4.text: Analyzed psychology and bubbles in speculative stock and housing markets.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-founded index business
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Karl Case and Allan Weiss, founded Case Shiller Weiss to develop index applications.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Yale
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began long research and teaching service, later becoming Sterling Professor and emeritus.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Excess-volatility study
strings.timeline.t7.text: Tested whether subsequent dividends could justify stock-price fluctuations.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Doctorate and Minnesota appointment
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned MIT’s doctorate and began his first faculty job studying expectations and markets.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completed Michigan degree
strings.timeline.t9.text: Earned his bachelor’s before graduate study at MIT.
